title: Intentional Weakness: How Craigslist and Southwest built uncopyable strategies
summary: Jason Cohen argues that durable strategies come from interlocking decisions that include deliberate weaknesses, which create unique strengths competitors won't copy because nobody copies weaknesses. He uses Craigslist and Southwest Airlines as examples, then shows how to focus on the ICP and ignore out-of-scope customers.

principles.text: Pick weaknesses on purpose; they enable special strengths that would otherwise be impossible.
principles.quote: This is that weaknesses enable special strengths that otherwise wouldn't be possible, and this is what gives them a unique and very durable strategy.

principles.text: Competitors copy strengths, never weaknesses, so a strategy built on weaknesses is uncopyable.
principles.quote: You're not going to copy weaknesses only strengths. But as I've said multiple times now, the weaknesses created unique strengths. So if you're not willing to copy that too, you are not going to win on those strengths.

principles.text: A good strategy is a network of reinforcing decisions, which creates coherence inside the company.
principles.quote: his point is that a good strategy is a network of decisions that reinforce each other

principles.text: Craigslist's minimal, stagnant site is a strength: anyone can use it, it's fast, selection is big and cost is tiny.
principles.quote: So what we see here is that these weaknesses enable special strengths that other sites don't have.

principles.text: Focus everything (marketing, sales, site, product) on the ICP, who sees no weaknesses in you.
principles.quote: you have to focus on them. And by focus I mean everything, marketing, sales, the website, product development features, everything for the ideal customer and not for the whole addressable market.

principles.text: Make strengths and trade-offs clear and the addressable market will sign up too; ignore out-of-scope feature requests.
principles.quote: You have to know who is my out of scope customer who's addressable. So that you don't listen to the out of scope feature requests and bug reports and confusions, they will drag you to a place that's not your strategy.
